question: Assume the JTB definition of Knowledge, which suggests that "Knowledge is a Justified True Belief". If our only available epistemic states are Knowledge and Belief, what are the two problems JTB runs into? Ignore Gettier problems.

6.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: With only Knowledge and Belief available as epistemic states, justification for a target belief P has to itself be either a further belief or a piece of knowledge. If it is a belief, that belief is itself a candidate for justification under JTB, so you need a further belief Q to justify it, and then a further belief R to justify Q, and so on. That is the classic regress of justification: you never actually get a non-increasing chain of reasons, you just keep pushing the justificatory burden back.

The only way to stop the regress without generating new epistemic states is to stop at a belief that is taken as justified in itself, i.e. a foundational belief that is not itself justified by anything else. With JTB that means you end up treating some beliefs as justified by fiat, an arbitrary dogmatic stopping point. In other words you either face an infinite, never-terminating justificatory chain, or you accept an ungrounded, arbitrarily privileged set of foundational beliefs as the base of knowledge.

4.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: With only Knowledge and Belief in the inventory, any justification you offer for a candidate belief p has to itself be either something you know or something you believe. 

If the justifier is a piece of knowledge, then that piece of knowledge itself needs a justifier, and that justifier needs a justifier, and so on. You never get off the ground: every putative knowledge claim is held in place by another knowledge claim that is in turn in need of support. That is the classic regress of justification.

If you try to stop the regress you have to allow a justification that is not itself justified by further knowledge or belief. On the stated restriction that leaves you with having to posit a class of basic beliefs that are taken as a stopping point without themselves being justified by anything more secure. In practice that is just dogmatic foundationalism: some beliefs are declared epistemically basic and exempt from the JTB requirement, so the theory ends up treating justified true belief as knowledge only after smuggling in an arbitrary, unjustified foundation.

These are the two ways the JTB picture is forced into trouble when Knowledge and Belief are the only epistemic resources available.

1.text:
With JTB the space of belief ascriptions is Truth x Justification.

* T+J+ = Justified True Belief = Knowledge
* T+J- = Unjustified True Belief
* T-J+ = Justified False Belief
* T-J- = Unjustified False Belief

If the ontology of epistemic states is exhausted by Knowledge and Belief, Knowledge can only be occupied by the T+J+ cell and Belief has to be the residual category for the other three cells.

Hence the 2x2 table is collapsed into

K = T+J+
B = T+J-  v  T-J+  v  T-J-

and two distinct epistemic profiles become indistinguishable under the label 'Belief'.

1. Justification without truth. A justified false belief is epistemically good in the sense that the agent has done all of the epistemic work she can do, and it is typically rated higher than an unjustified false belief. On JTB with only K/B as resources T-J+ is forced into the undifferentiated class Belief, so justified error is epistemically indistinguishable from unjustified error. Justification ceases to be an epistemic marker as soon as the belief turns out false.

2. Truth without justification. An unjustified true belief is epistemically defective in the sense that the agent is lucky, the truth is accidental. T+J- is forced into the same undifferentiated class Belief as T-J+. So lucky true belief is epistemically indistinguishable from justified error. Truth ceases to be an epistemic marker as soon as justification is absent.

In effect the account cannot honour the independent epistemic value of justification when the belief is false, nor the independent epistemic defect of lack of justification when the belief is true. The three non-knowledge cells are lumped together as mere Belief so we lose the distinct states of justified false belief and of unjustified true belief. That is the need for a finer taxonomy of epistemic states than the Knowledge/Belief dichotomy.

3.text:
Under the traditional tripartite analysis Knowledge = Belief + True + Justified
knowledge is a proper species of belief.

Truth x Justification gives four logical cells

* T & J
* T & ~J
* ~T & J
* ~T & ~J

On JTB the first cell is Knowledge by definition. If Knowledge and
Belief are the only two epistemic kinds that are available the remaining
three cells all have to be called Belief. Belief is therefore a
heterogeneous disjunction.

* *Justified false belief* ~T & J.  The belief is justified and so,
ceteris paribus, epistemically meritorious, but it is false and so on
JTB it is not knowledge. With only Knowledge vs Belief left there is
nowhere to put it except Belief. Justification for false beliefs is
hence epistemically invisible: a justified false belief is on a par
with an unjustified false belief and justification makes no difference
to the state that is ascribed.

* *Unjustified true belief* T & ~J.  The belief is true but it is
true only by luck, it is not justified and so on JTB it is not
knowledge. With only Knowledge vs Belief left it too has to be called
Belief. Truth for unjustified beliefs is hence epistemically invisible:
a lucky true belief is on a par with a justified false belief and with
an unjustified false belief and truth makes no difference to the state
that is ascribed.

Hence with only Knowledge and Belief as categories JTB cannot keep
justification and truth independently trackable. There is no distinct
state of justified non-knowledge and no distinct state of true non-
knowledge, so justification and truth can only be recognised in the
conjunction of justified true belief, i.e. in knowledge itself. Justified
belief without knowledge and true belief without knowledge are both
forced into the undifferentiated residue ‘mere belief’.

5.text:
With a JTB analysis knowledge is true belief + justification. If the taxonomy is
forced to be binary, Knowledge vs mere Belief, everything that is not
Knowledge has to be called Belief.

That means the sub-knowledge space is not represented at all.

* Justified false belief. A belief can be properly justified and still be false.
On JTB it is not Knowledge because it is not true. On a Knowledge/Belief
binary it is just Belief. It is therefore lumped together with unjustified
false belief. The epistemic difference between a well-justified error and a
bare, unjustified error is lost.

* Unjustified true belief. A belief can be true by luck/accident and be
unjustified. On JTB it is not Knowledge because it is not justified. On a
Knowledge/Belief binary it is just Belief. It is therefore lumped together
with justified false belief and with unjustified false belief. The
epistemic difference between a true belief that is lucky and a false belief,
justified or not, is lost.

In effect the binary scheme makes justification irrelevant for false
beliefs and makes truth irrelevant for non-knowledge beliefs. We have no
place for a justified but false state that is epistemically better than
mere false belief, and no place for a true but unjustified state that is
epistemically better than a false belief. The classic fine-grained states
justified false belief and unjustified true belief collapse into the single
category ‘Belief’.

2.text:
With only the two labels Knowledge and Belief the JTB analysis is forced to be

K = justified & true & belief
B = not K

so that every mental state which is not a justified true belief has to be called a belief. 
That makes Belief a heterogeneous grab-bag and it is for that reason that the
binary Knowledge / Belief taxonomy cannot be maintained.

* Justified False Belief.  A belief can be justified and still be false. 
JFB is not knowledge because knowledge on JTB requires truth, but it is
justified.  On a Knowledge/Belief only taxonomy it has to be labelled
‘belief’.  Belief is therefore being used to cover a state that is
justified, i.e. belief is no longer coextensive with mere lack of
justification.

* Unjustified True Belief.  A belief can be true and still be
unjustified.  UTB is not knowledge because knowledge on JTB requires
justification, but it is true.  On a Knowledge/Belief only taxonomy it
has to be labelled ‘belief’.  Belief is therefore being used to cover a
state that is true, i.e. belief is no longer coextensive with mere lack
of truth.

Hence with the two labels Belief is forced to be the disjunction
{JFB , UTB , unjustified false belief}.  It is simultaneously used to mark
lack of truth and lack of justification, so the Knowledge/Belief
distinction conflates justified with unjustified belief and true with
false belief.  That is the in-principle incoherence of keeping a strict
binary taxonomy while analysing knowledge as justified true belief.

2.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The question is about the consequences of restricting the epistemic taxonomy to just Knowledge vs Belief while retaining JTB = Justified True Belief.

Public round 0 consensus from Colleagues 1,2,3,5: JTB yields a 2x2 Truth × Justification space:
T+J+ = Knowledge
T+J- = Unjustified True Belief
T-J+ = Justified False Belief
T-J- = Unjustified False Belief

With only Knowledge and Belief as labels, Knowledge can only occupy T+J+ and everything else must be called Belief, i.e. B = T+J- ∨ T-J+ ∨ T-J-. Belief becomes a heterogeneous grab-bag.

Two distinct problems are then repeatedly identified:
1. Justification without truth is invisible. T-J+ Justified False Belief is epistemically meritorious by justification but non-knowledge by falsity. Forced into the undifferentiated Belief class it becomes indistinguishable from T-J- Unjustified False Belief. Justification ceases to mark an epistemic difference once the belief is false; there is no distinct state of justified non-knowledge.
2. Truth without justification is invisible. T+J- Unjustified True Belief is true but only by luck, non-knowledge by lack of justification. Forced into Belief it becomes indistinguishable from T-J+ Justified False Belief and T-J- Unjustified False Belief. Truth ceases to mark an epistemic difference once justification is absent; there is no distinct state of true non-knowledge.

In effect JTB cannot keep justification and truth independently trackable with a binary taxonomy; the three non-knowledge cells collapse, losing the fine-grained states of justified false belief and unjustified true belief.

Disagreement/minority view: Colleagues 4 and 6 raise a different pair of problems, about the regress of justification when justifiers can only be Knowledge or Belief. That would force an infinite chain of justifiers or an arbitrary dogmatic foundational stopping point with basic beliefs justified by fiat. This is a regress/foundationalism worry rather than the heterogeneity of Belief. I am keeping it as an alternative interpretation, but the majority argument about conflation of JFB and UTB fits the wording about available epistemic states more directly. Unresolved whether the regress concern is intended or a misreading of the state inventory restriction.

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The question is about the cost of keeping only two epistemic kinds, Knowledge and Belief, while analysing Knowledge as Justified True Belief. Truth × Justification gives four logical cells: T+J+, T+J-, T-J+, T-J-. On JTB T+J+ = Knowledge by definition.

Colleagues 1,2,3,5 converge on the same structural problem: the remaining three cells must all be labelled ‘Belief’. Belief therefore becomes a heterogeneous residue:

* T-J+ Justified False Belief. A belief can be justified yet false, so by JTB it is not Knowledge. With only K/B it has to be called Belief, so a well-justified error is lumped with unjustified error. Justification is epistemically invisible for false beliefs; the epistemic merit of being justified is lost once truth fails.

* T+J- Unjustified True Belief. A belief can be true yet unjustified, so by JTB it is not Knowledge. With only K/B it also has to be called Belief, so a lucky true belief is lumped with justified false belief and unjustified false belief. Truth is epistemically invisible for non-knowledge beliefs; the epistemic defect of lack of justification is lost once justification is absent.

Hence the binary taxonomy cannot keep justification and truth independently trackable. There is no distinct state for justified non-knowledge and no distinct state for true non-knowledge; justification and truth are only recognised in the conjunction T+J+. That is the need for a finer taxonomy than Knowledge/Belief.

Disagreement noted: Colleagues 4 and 6 frame the problem differently as a regress/foundationalism problem. Because with only Knowledge and Belief, any justifier for P must itself be a Knowledge or a Belief. If a Belief, it itself needs justification, leading to an infinite regress; to stop the regress you must posit foundational beliefs that are justified by fiat, i.e. dogmatic foundationalism. This is a different diagnosis than the heterogeneous-Belief/ loss-of-tracking diagnosis, and it is not widely shared in the current round.

Current leaning: the consensus two problems are the collapse of Justified False Belief and Unjustified True Belief into the undifferentiated Belief category, with the resulting loss of independent epistemic value of justification for false beliefs and of truth for unjustified beliefs. Unresolved: whether the regress/foundationalism point is a genuine second problem under the stated “only two epistemic states” constraint or a separate meta-problem about justification.

B = T+ & J-  v  T- & J+  v  T- & J-.

With JTB and a Knowledge / Belief only taxonomy the Truth × Justification matrix collapses to

* T+J+ = Knowledge by definition
* T+J- = Unjustified True Belief
* T-J+ = Justified False Belief
* T-J- = Unjustified False Belief

If Knowledge and Belief are exhaustive K can occupy only T+J+ and Belief is forced to be the residual

K = T+J+
B = T+J- ∨ T-J+ ∨ T-J-

Belief is then a heterogeneous grab-bag and justification and truth can only be recognised together in Knowledge.

1. Justification without truth is epistemically invisible. 
T-J+ is a justified false belief. On JTB it is not knowledge because it is false, but it is epistemically meritorious by justification and ceteris paribus better than T-J- unjustified false belief. With only K/B available T-J+ has nowhere to go except Belief, so it is lumped with T-J-. Justification therefore ceases to mark an epistemic difference once truth fails: a well-justified error is indistinguishable in kind from a bare error, so there is no distinct state of justified non-knowledge.

2. Truth without justification is epistemically invisible. 
T+J- is an unjustified true belief. On JTB it is not knowledge because it lacks justification, but it is true and ceteris paribus better than falsehood. With only K/B available T+J- must also be labelled Belief, so it is lumped with T-J+ and T-J-. Truth therefore ceases to mark an epistemic difference once justification is absent: a lucky true belief is indistinguishable in kind from justified error and from unjustified error, so there is no distinct state of true non-knowledge.

Hence justification and truth can only be tracked in their conjunction T+J+ i.e. in Knowledge itself. The fine-grained states justified false belief and unjustified true belief collapse into the undifferentiated residue ‘mere belief’, and Belief is used simultaneously to mark lack of truth and lack of justification. That is the specific loss of granularity forced by keeping a strict Knowledge/Belief dichotomy while analysing knowledge as justified true belief.
